candidate_facts.text: The United States intervened in the Korean War to prevent the spread of communism.
The U.S. intervention in the Korean War aligned with the Cold War strategy of containment.
The Korean War was the first major military conflict of the Cold War.
The Korean War served as a test of the containment doctrine.
The Korean War was the first test of the Cold War doctrine of containment.
The Korean War demonstrated the U.S. commitment to stopping communist expansion without triggering a global conflict.
General Douglas MacArthur proposed expanding the war into China and using nuclear weapons.
MacArthur's proposal prompted internal debates about containing communism versus risking a global conflict.
The internal debates ultimately led to the war being confined to the Korean Peninsula.
The U.S. believed that if South Korea fell, communist leaders would be emboldened to threaten other nations closer to the West.
The belief that South Korea's fall would embolden communist leaders reinforced the rationale for U.S. intervention.
